mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have risen steadily for three consecutive weeks, indicating restored commuting routines that generate incidental retail trips along commute paths, which will keep RETAIL_REC on an upward trajectory over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to average higher over the next 28 days than the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their weekly upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 7.4 to 3.7 over four weeks; once it crosses below 3.0, it signals that stay-at-home behavior has substantially unwound, freeing discretionary time for retail and recreation trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of RESIDENTIAL crossing below the 3.0 threshold, or RESIDENTIAL stalls above threshold while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous recovery of PARKS and TRANSIT reflects relaxed restrictions on outdoor and public movement, which historically precedes a broader rebound in retail and recreation activity over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -24.1 to -15.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next 28 days even though PARKS and TRANSIT continue to improve, indicating decoupling from reopening dynamics.

mechanism_narrative: The joint acceleration of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recovery (both improving by 2-4 points weekly) compounds to produce a stronger near-term boost to RETAIL_REC than either series alone, because commuters combine work trips with transit-adjacent shopping within a single week.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by more than 2 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within the following week when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT jointly improve by more than 2 points, or rises even when only one series improves.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has plateaued and partially reversed (8.4 to 4.7) as winter weather reduces outdoor appeal, shifting discretionary recreation time indoors toward retail venues over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 8.4 to 4.7 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS decline, or PARKS decline is accompanied by a simultaneous RETAIL_REC decline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM growth has decelerated from +2.3 to -0.9 points week-on-week, suggesting essential-goods demand is saturating; once weekly growth turns negative, consumers reallocate spending toward discretionary retail and recreation within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change turns negative after prior positive growth
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM weekly increments shrank from 2.3 to 0.9 to -0.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM's weekly change turning negative, or RETAIL_REC rises while GROCERY_PHARM growth remains positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained four-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 7.4 to 3.7) indicates a persistent unwinding of at-home confinement behavior that structurally supports higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks regardless of short-term fluctuations.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to average higher over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise above their respective pre-period deficits by more than 5 points while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously falls below 4.0, this triple pattern signals a full institutional reopening that sharply accelerates RETAIL_REC growth within two weeks, exceeding the effect of any single series.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve >5 points from t-3w while RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 3.7 at t-0w, WORKPLACES improved from -20.0 to -14.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not accelerate beyond its prior trend within two weeks of the joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT/RESIDENTIAL threshold being met.
